title: Let Us Adore the Grace That Seeks
description: Let Us Adore the Grace That Seeks in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 21, “The Lord's call to his children. 2Cor 6:17,18”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let us a-dore the grace that seeks To draw our hearts a-bove! At-tend, 'tis God the Sa-vior speaks, And ev-ery word is love.

lines: Let us adore the grace that seeks
To draw our hearts above!
Attend, 'tis God the Savior speaks,
And every word is love.
Though filled with awe, before his throne
Each angel veils his face;
He claims a people for his own
Amongst our sinful race.
Careless, awhile, they live in sin,
Enslaved to Satan's pow'r;
But they obey the call divine,
In his appointed hour.
Come forth, he says, no more pursue
The paths that lead to death;
Look up, a bleeding Savior view,
Look, and be saved by faith.
My sons and daughters you shall be
Through the atoning blood;
And you shall claim, and find, in me,
A Father, and a God."
Lord, speak these words to every heart,
By thine all-powerful voice;
That we may now from sin depart,
And make thy love our choice.
If now, we learn to seek thy face
By Christ, the living way;
We'll praise thee for this hour of grace,
Through an eternal day.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
